text: Sorted can order anything, as long as you tell it what to sort by.
We start with four words of different lengths.
Sorted always returns a new list, leaving the original untouched.
Key equals len means sort by the length of each word, not alphabetically.
Notice we pass len itself, not len parentheses — the function, not a call to it.
So fig, kiwi, apple, banana. Shortest to longest.
For tuples, a lambda picks which part to sort on.
p bracket one grabs the age, and reverse equals True flips it to highest first.
Any function works as a key, so you can sort by anything you can compute.
Cat at forty, amy at thirty, ben at twenty-five.
Max takes the very same key argument, and so do most Python functions.
So the oldest person falls out with no sorting at all.
